flawed_step: Lines 0016–0017: the proof incorrectly claims that σ[..i] fixes the failure of the eventuality F(P1C ∨ P2C). A finite prefix cannot establish that the requested event never occurs later.
counterexample: Let σ(t)={P1E,P2E} for every t≥0, with P1C and P2C always false. Then σ violates the property. Choose i=0, so the proposed bad prefix is [{P1E,P2E}]. Extend it to σ′ by σ′(0)={P1E,P2E}, σ′(1)={P1C}, and σ′(t)=∅ for all t≥2. At time 0, F(P1C∨P2C) is true because P1C holds at time 1; at every later time the antecedent P1E∧P2E is false. Thus σ′ satisfies the global property despite extending the alleged bad prefix.
assessment_summary: The concrete extension refutes the relied-upon claim that σ[..i] is a bad prefix. The eventuality's failure cannot be certified at finite time, so the safety proof is invalid.
